data.reasoning: The package is a standard Python AUR package with pinned source (SHA-256 checksum from official GitHub releases), standard build tools (python -m build, python -m installer), and no suspicious commands or network operations. The disagreement between reports was caused solely by a tool error (HTTP 400 API failure) in the qwen model when reviewing .gitignore, not by any actual security concern. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all files and correctly identified them as safe.
data.disagreement_analysis: The qwen model encountered an API error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError) when attempting to audit .gitignore, resulting in an inconclusive verdict for that file and consequently an overall inconclusive result. The deepseek model successfully audited the same file and found it to be a standard AUR .gitignore with no malicious content. This is a tool failure, not a genuine security disagreement.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to review .gitignore due to API error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError)
learnings: Tool errors (API failures, timeouts) should be distinguished from genuine security inconclusiveness - a failed audit should not trigger an overall inconclusive verdict when other models successfully complete the audit
Implement retry logic or fallback mechanisms when LLM API calls fail, rather than marking files as inconclusive

When one model has a tool error and another successfully completes the audit with a safe verdict on the same files, the system should recognize this as a tool failure rather than model disagreement requiring escalation
